title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds autotune for batching and caching defaults, exposes quantization profiles, and introduces unit-economics (UEcon) tooling to evaluate per-token cost impact. No breaking changes.
description: Motivation: Production inference costs are highly sensitive to batching/caching defaults and quantization choices. Customers repeatedly ask for sane defaults and automated recommendations that trade off latency vs unit cost. This PR implements an initial autotune path that (1) sets workload-aware batching and KV-cache defaults, (2) exposes quantization profiles per model family, and (3) adds a UEcon tooling CLI and API to estimate per-request token cost under different configs. Summary: - Add runtime/autotune module to compute defaults based on recent request histograms and SLO targets. - Add quant-profiles metadata and selection logic in model registry and serving runtime. - Add tools/uecon service + CLI to simulate unit economics, produce per-route recommendations, and generate a minimal UI payload for Console. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-3421) [x] Tests covering autotune heuristics and quant selection [x] Benchmarks showing ~12-18% median cost reduction on sampled workloads [x] Docs + Console payload wiring [ ] Post-merge: schedule 1-week canary on dedicated tier Details: - Autotune computes batch_size, max_batch_wait_ms, and cache_prefix_ttl by ingesting the last 6 hours of request size and arrival-rate histograms (default fallback is conservative static values). - Quant profiles: added JSON descriptors per model (fp16, int8-ql4, int8-ql8, gptq-lite) with expected perf/cost/quality deltas; runtime picks the highest-compression profile that meets the configured quality threshold. - UEcon tooling: a local CLI (tools/uecon/cli) that ingests sample traces and runs Monte Carlo simulations across configs, outputting expected cost/token, p95 latency, and expected quality delta. Migration: model registry entries include a new "quant_profiles" key; the runtime tolerates missing keys and falls back to existing behavior. Security: no secrets changes. Observability: added autotune.metrics.{decision_count,applied_defaults} and uecon.simulation_{runs,median_cost}. See ENG-3421 for design and ENG-3489 for benchmarking notes.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice work — overall approach LGTM. Two concerns: 1) default TTL for cache_prefix seems low for sparse workloads, can we make it workload-adaptive? 2) quant profile schema needs a quality confidence field.
Maya Chen: Thanks Arjun — addressed in commit 'workload-adaptive-ttl' and added 'quality_confidence' to the schema. Updated tests to cover edge cases.
Liam O'Connor: Tests look good, but the UEcon CLI runtime is slow for large traces. Suggest streaming the simulation and adding a --sample-rate option.
Maya Chen: Added --sample-rate and a streaming mode in the latest patch. Benchmarks: full trace run from 18m -> 2.2m seconds -> 3.8s with sampling 1% (results pushed to ENG-3489).
Sofia Martinez: Telemetry names are fine. Please ensure we don't expose internal simulation payloads in Console — sanitize before sending.
Maya Chen: Console payload now only includes aggregated recommendation summaries and non-identifying simulation metrics.
Arjun Patel: CI flake on windows build for tools/uecon; rerun once CI fixes. Approving after green CI.
notes: Canary: schedule 1-week on dedicated-small region and monitor autotune.metrics.applied_defaults and uecon.simulation_median_cost. Pin rollback runbook in ENG-3421.
changelog_excerpt: Autotune: compute workload-aware batching and cache defaults; Quant profiles: introduce model-level compression/quality metadata; UEcon: add simulation tooling for per-token cost estimates.
